what_it_shows: FossilEra fossils: 25 categories by taxon/kind (Amber 117, Ammonite 160, Dinosaur 196, Fish 92, Insects 82, Shark Teeth 133, Petrified Wood 181, Stromatolites 72, Trilobites 198, Plant, Mammals, Echinoderms, Coral, Gastropods, Belemnites, Crabs); price filters up to $5,000; fossilization types explained

FossilEra minerals: first facets Specimens (1484) / Polished (1481) / Pendants (61), then ~207 mineral-species categories (Quartz 308, Calcite 202, Jasper 251, Agates 280, Amethyst, Fluorite, Pyrite, Geodes, Opals); 2,985 items $2-$29,000

FossilEra meteorites: Achondrites, Chondrites, HED, Iron, Lunar, Martian, Mesosiderites, Pallasites, Tektites and Impactites, Pendants; buyer guide stony / iron / stony-iron with famous irons Canyon Diablo, Sikhote-Alin, Gibeon, Campo del Cielo; 692 items $3-$6,950
eBay.de Mineralien & Fossilien: five children Mineral, Fossil, Heilstein (healing stone), Edelstein (gemstone), Meteorit
Webmineral New Dana: 78 numbered classes (01 Native Elements, 02 Sulfides, 03 Sulfosalts, 04 Simple Oxides ... 78 Unclassified silicates) mapped to old Dana I-IX incl. IX Organic Minerals

Geolitho marketplace/auction for collectors: object-type filter Fossil, Mineral, Gestein (rock), Extraterrestrisch (Meteoriten), Historischer Gegenstand, Buch/Magazin; aesthetic/quality score 1-5, +image +analysis, price range

N's Mineral (JP) category index: meteorites (iron, pallasite, stony, lunar, martian, carbonaceous, HED, Libyan glass), native elements, locality-led categories (Tsumeb, fluorite by country), then A-to-Z by species in gojuon order, gem species (emerald, tanzanite, spinel, ruby-sapphire), lab-grown crystals, collection supplies

Mineraly.fr: seven top categories by presentation form: Cristaux (sur gangue, geodes et druses, cristallisation), Roches (agregats, brutes), Ornement (pierres polies), Fossiles (bruts, polis), Objets (coeurs, spheres, oeufs, tranches...), Bijoux, Meteorites; separate facets for mineral type, country and collections

Tokyo Science: top categories Fossil, Mineral (specimens, polished items, gems), Rock (rock sample sets), bottled sand samples, Meteorite (stony, iron, stony-iron, tektite), paleontological reconstruction models

Le Comptoir Geologique catalogues: Mineraux, Fossiles, Gemmes, Pierres roulees (tumbled), Bijoux, Modeles cristallographiques, Oeufs et spheres polis, Meteorites, Materiel, Livres; with encyclopedia and lexicon

HS 9705 collections and collectors' pieces: 970510 archaeological/ethnographic/historical; 970521 human specimens; 970522 extinct or endangered species; 970529 zoological, botanical, mineralogical, anatomical, paleontological (other); 970531/39 numismatic; Chapter 97 note 1(c) excludes pearls and precious/semi-precious stones (7101-7103)

GBIF/Darwin Core basis of record: Living, Preserved (herbarium sheet, jar lot), Fossil Specimen (body fossil, coprolite, gastrolith, ichnofossil, petrified wood), Material Citation, Human and Machine Observation

Strunz classification: 10 compositional classes (elements, sulfides, halides, oxides, nitrates+carbonates, borates, sulfates, phosphates, silicates, organic compounds) subdivided into divisions, families, groups by chemistry and structure; IMA Nickel-Strunz v10

GIA pearl buyer guide: seven pearl value factors (size, shape, color, luster, surface, nacre, matching); eight basic shapes; natural or cultured pearls; South Sea, Tahitian, akoya, freshwater varieties

GIA report types: natural diamond grading (4Cs), diamond origin, natural colored diamond, laboratory-grown diamond (LGDS), colored gemstone identification (species, natural or synthetic, treatment, origin), pearl classification (7 factors)

GemSelect: 130+ gem species A-Z (sapphire 5067 in stock, garnet 5962, topaz 3699, tourmaline 2568) plus cross-cutting main categories (Top Grade, Drilled gems/briolettes/beads, Matching Pairs, Cabochon); each species sold as singles, pairs, lots, faceted or cabochon

GemSelect sapphire page: facets weight, size, clarity, price, treatment; colour sub-pages (blue, pink, yellow...); form tabs Single / Pairs / Lots / Faceted / Cabochons; listings give carat, shape, clarity, size, price

Gem Rock Auctions: Buy-it-now categories by species (Diamond, Colored Diamonds, Sapphire, Ruby, Emerald, Tourmaline, Garnet, Tanzanite, Spinel, Aquamarine); Shop by type: Cabochons, Pairs, Rough Raw Gemstones (facet-grade rough), Mineral Specimens; certified (GFCO, AIGS, Lotus) and unheated filters

TOP STONE (JP) loose gems: category by species (sapphire page with colour/origin sub-types such as cornflower blue, Montana, Kashmir purple), filters category / brand / price band / colour / sales type / stock; listings carry origin, lab certificate (LOTUS, ソ付), carat and size

Conchology Inc: 118,655 shells for sale browsed by family (320 families, 6,839 species), with popular families Pectinidae, Fossils, Fakes, Brachiopoda; size filters, marine vs other habitat; dealer-collector star system

Loving Coastal Living seashells: categories Collector's Shells (documented species with collection details), Bulk Seashells (craft and wedding use) and species groups such as scallops, cone shells, cowrie, conch, murex, volute

Oddities For Sale: Natural Specimens parent category; Taxidermy and Bones sub-category (31 items: skulls by species, taxidermy mounts, osteoderms, nerite shells, dried leeches); sold as curiosities, decor
Collector mineral size classes by longest dimension: thumbnail under 1.5 in, miniature 1.5-2.5, small cabinet 2.5-4, cabinet 4-6, large cabinet 6-10; stated as a convention, not a grading system

Natural History Museum London mineralogy collections: Meteorites, Minerals (species-systematic, with gems), Ocean bottom deposits, Ores, Rocks (approx 177,000); about 500,000 rocks, gems and minerals incl. 5,000 meteorites

Cornerstone Educational Supply: rock collection sold as three kits by rock class (igneous, sedimentary, metamorphic) with named rock kinds (granite, basalt, obsidian, sandstone, shale, coquina, marble, slate, gneiss, quartzite) in a 48-specimen set
